title: Design an Unreliable Device Dispatch and Reconciliation System
prompt:
Design a control center that sends energy-reduction commands to smart devices. Devices may miss, reject, or fail to execute a command; telemetry can be delayed, duplicated, or out of order. Follow-up commands must account for uncertain device state.

Define the command and telemetry interfaces and what the controller reports to operators. Explain retries, expiry, reconciliation, group-level safety limits, and recovery. Distinguish acknowledgement from observed execution.

response.placeholder: Start with an authoritative command ledger and the distinction between intent, delivery, execution, and observation.
response.reference_answer:
## State contract

Every command has a durable ID, target selector, desired effect, expiry, policy version, and per-device state. Sent, acknowledged, accepted, executed, rejected, expired, and unknown are distinct states. A delivery acknowledgement never proves the physical action occurred.

## Ingestion and reconciliation

Commands and telemetry append to durable, partitioned logs. The ingestion path deduplicates by device event ID and retains event time, arrival time, and a sequence or epoch where available. A reconciliation worker joins expected outcomes with acknowledgements and telemetry using a bounded-lateness watermark. It produces idempotent transitions and keeps contradictory or late evidence as diagnostics instead of overwriting a newer decision blindly.

## Safety and recovery

Retries apply only while the command is eligible and the group safety budget permits it. The controller uses conservative behavior for unknown device state, such as withholding a follow-up increase until reconciliation or expiry. Commands and observations are replayable after a controller failure; leases and state versions prevent an old worker from reviving a superseded command.

## Operations

Measure delivery, acknowledgement, observed-execution, unknown-outcome, duplicate-event, late-event, reconciliation-lag, and safety-cap rates by device class and region. Operators can inspect the evidence behind a device state and override policy through an auditable command, not by mutating telemetry history.
